sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was reduced significantly: FY26 EBIT guidance is USD -1.5bn to +1.0bn, compared to FY25 EBIT of USD 3.5bn. Management explicitly cites industry overcapacity and Red Sea reopening scenarios as headwinds. The share buyback was also reduced from USD 2.0bn in 2025 to USD 1.0bn for the next 12 months, reflecting a more cautious approach. While Q4 results were in line with expectations, the forward outlook is clearly lower.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 revenue USD 13.3bn, down 8.7% YoY. FY25 revenue USD 54.0bn, down 2.7% YoY.
summary.eps: Not disclosed. Underlying profit for FY25 was USD 6,095m, down from USD 6,232m in FY24.
summary.guidance: FY26 underlying EBITDA USD 4.5bn to 7.0bn, underlying EBIT USD -1.5bn to +1.0bn, FCF ≥ USD 3bn. Global container volume growth expected 2-4%.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 EBIT margin 0.9% (down from 14.0% in Q4 2024). FY25 EBIT margin 6.5% (down from 11.7% in FY24).
key_risks: Industry overcapacity from new vessel deliveries
Potential full Red Sea reopening in 2026, which would add further capacity
Freight rate decline: Ocean rates down 23% YoY in Q4
Trade tensions and tariff environment impacting US-China volumes
Logistics & Services still below 6% EBIT margin target
key_opportunities: Gemini cooperation delivering cost savings of USD 820-1,100m annually
Terminals record performance with 20% revenue growth and 31% EBIT growth in FY25
Logistics & Services margin improvement: 4.8% FY25 vs 3.6% FY24
Strong balance sheet with net cash of USD 2.9bn to weather downturn
Organizational cost reduction of USD 180m annually

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: CEO Vincent Clerc stated: 'The lower level reflects the higher level of uncertainty and the lower rate environment that we are headed into in 2026.'
